messages:
incidents-bot: Paging: SLO breach detected for streaming API in eu-west2. p99 latency > 5s for last 10m, error rate up 1.8%. Auto-run diagnostics triggered: net-trace + flow-check. Incident severity: SEV2. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/2183456789 :rotating_light:

maya: acked. I'm oncall for infra. grabbing dashboards (latency, retransmits, nat usage).

sam: oncall handoff received. joining now. any customer-facing page up?

maya: notifying support to hold on outbound customer comms until we confirm scope. initial look: p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~6.2s, streaming stalls observed in tail tokens. Streaming stalls correlate with bursts in TLS handshakes.

alex: checking VPC egress path. I see spikes in NAT gateway connection counts and high tcp_retransmit for some hosts in az-b/az-c. suspect ephemeral port exhaustion or cross-AZ routing flaps.

nina: running quick netstat on a troubled host: ```
# netstat -an | grep :443 | wc -l
> 15200
# ss -s
TCP: inuse 15300 orphan 0 tw 21000 alloc 54000 mem 2.3G
```

raj: can you grab `ss -t -o state established '( dport = :https )'` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` from one of the worker nodes?

alex: pasted outputs into pastebin: https://paste.redwood.internal/abc123 - conntrack ~ 120k, conntrack table near max (130k). NAT ephemeral ports showing heavy reuse.

maya: that would explain TLS handshake spikes (clients failing and retrying). also seeing DNS retries ~300/s in eu-west2 from app hosts -> increases connection churn.

sam: running tcpdump on host (short capture): ```
# tcpdump -i eth0 -n port 443 and host 10.20.30.45 -c 200 -w /tmp/cap.pcap
# tshark -r /tmp/cap.pcap -q -z conv,tcp
``` Observed many SYN retransmits and duplicate ACKs.

netops-bot: Noted: AWS NAT gateway metrics show SNAT allocation pressure in eu-west2b between 10:14-10:28 UTC. Possible burst from Canary job earlier.

nina: Canary job? oh right, there was a large reindex job kicked off by analytics around 10:10 that fanout'd to many worker pools.

maya: immediate mitigation: 1) throttle analytics reindex fanout, 2) spin up additional NAT capacity in eu-west2 via on-demand NAT gateways, 3) temporarily prefer locally pinned models to avoid cross-AZ egress. I'll apply 1 and 3 now.

sam: apply runbook step: ```
# scale nat
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-xyz --allocation-id eipalloc-abc
# or enable additional NAT instances via autoscale
```

alex: I've pushed a routing policy change to prefer AZ-local egress for streaming pods (canary to 10% traffic) — watch for routing errors.

nina: throttled analytics job at 10:22 UTC. Confirmed job now running at reduced concurrency.

raj: conntrack free increased after throttling. conntrack now 67k and falling. TLS handshake retries dropping. p99 dropping to ~2.1s at 10:30 UTC.

maya: netops created a second NAT GW at 10:25. SNAT allocation stabilized. netops-bot: NAT capacity check OK. :white_check_mark:

sam: customer impact: intermittent streaming stalls for ~10% of requests between 10:10-10:28 UTC, affecting long-running chat sessions and large prompt tokenization. We should mark degraded and notify affected paid customers. prepping a short status update.

alex: still some residual p99 spikes tied to cross-zone TLS handshakes when fallback routing triggers. planning a full route-policy rollback if instability persists.

nina: collecting packet captures for 10:10-10:35 window and uploading to secure S3: s3://redwood-incident-eu/2183456789/caps/

maya: action items summarized: [1] Confirm all NAT additions healthy (netops), [2] Keep analytics throttle until next maintenance (data eng), [3] Investigate DNS dependency causing retries (platform), [4] Postmortem owner: alex, ETA initial draft 24h.

raj: quick DNS note — resolver health looked fine, but a spike of SERVFAIL from an internal edge-proxy caused clients to switch endpoints and retrigger TLS handshakes. opening follow-up for proxy team.

sam: on-call handoff in 30m to raj for follow-up. I'm taking the bridge for immediate customer comms and PG. maya, can you pick up next ops shift at 11:00?

maya: yep I'll take ops at 11. documenting mitigations in the incident doc. final status: SLO now restored to target at p99 <3s, streaming tail regressions mostly resolved. leaving the thread open for root cause analysis. :heavy_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Auto-close guard: thread will remain open until postmortem filed. Paging done.

sam: leaving note for postmortem: correlate analytics job change with NAT allocation pressure; consider autoscaling conntrack and ephemeral port space, and add pre-flight check for large fanouts.

alex: grabbing logs for the proxy that returned SERVFAILs. will attach to PM.

raj: taking over follow-ups. will coordinate with platform and proxy owners. thumbs-up to all for quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
